name: Tailwear — The Appendage Expression Movement
creator: Geneware community originating in the Lakeshore Stack, Tier 2
description: A geneware-driven fashion movement centered on functional and decorative tail appendages — prehensile, bioluminescent, feathered, scaled, or articulated mechanical hybrids — as the primary personal expression statement. Unlike earlier novelty geneware, Tailwear practitioners treat the appendage as a permanent identity marker requiring years of integration therapy and movement training, with dedicated 'tail culture' spaces adapted for their physical needs. The movement developed its own vocabulary of tail-position etiquette and social signaling that outsiders struggle to read.
cultural_impact: Tailwear forced significant public infrastructure adaptation debates — seating, transit, workplace accommodation — making geneware body modification a mainstream civil rights question rather than a fringe curiosity. It also established geneware identity communities as politically organized for the first time.
controversy: Corporate geneware providers were accused of deliberately engineering dependence and expensive maintenance cycles into tail modifications. Several Tier 1 black-market tail procedures resulted in severe nerve damage, prompting underground mutual aid networks to develop their own aftercare protocols.
story_hooks: A Tailwear community leader discovers their geneware provider has been harvesting proprietary biological data from every procedure — and selling it to a Spire longevity research program.

A the Gray Zone child receives an unlicensed tail modification from a black-market clinic; when it starts failing, their family must choose between the expensive licensed fix and the dangerous underground repair network.
A Tier 4 corporate building refuses accommodation for a Tailwear employee — the resulting legal case becomes the most-followed tribunal feed in Meridian history.
